title: cache-rehydration-model-variant-cost-normalization
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Background: The KV prefix/cache subsystem can rehydrate full generated outputs for later requests. We currently store serialized output blobs without enforcing or preserving a deterministic billing provenance payload. This leads to incorrect billing when a cached output generated by a higher-cost model variant is later served to requests that would have used a lower-cost variant (or a different customer tier), or when a cache hit crosses tenant/route boundaries.

Problem statement: There are cases where cache hits result in mismatched per-token debits and incorrect ledger attribution. Examples: a) Customer A generates a long response on model:open-large and it is cached; later Customer B (or Customer A on a different route with lower tier) hits the same cache key and is served the cached blob but only charged at the lower-route unit price. b) A fallback path (low-latency tier) serves cached outputs generated by the higher-throughput reserved pool and billing uses the serving route price rather than original generation cost. These lead to undercharging or incorrect accounting and break unit-cost SLAs and revenue guarantees.

Goal: Ensure that any cached-rehydrated response that incurs token-generation cost is billed deterministically and auditable to: original generator provenance (model variant, snapshot id, token counts), owning tenant or a safe fallback billing policy; and that the cache/metering system never double-bills or creates orphaned credits. Implement schema, runtime checks, ledger anchors, and tests so cached hits are cost-normalized and traceable.
acceptance_criteria: Cache entries must include provenance metadata: generator_model, generator_snapshot, generated_input_token_count, generated_output_token_count, generation_request_id, generation_timestamp

On cache hit, billing system charges either (A) original generation cost recorded in the provenance OR (B) the configured normalization policy (e.g., bill max(original_cost, serving_route_cost)). The policy is configurable per-org and per-route.

Shared/global cache entries must be marked non-billable unless the entry carries explicit per-tenant billing consent. Serving such entries for different tenants must trigger re-generation or apply configured surcharge policy.
The ledger must anchor the cache-hit debit to a single atomic transaction that includes cache provenance id to avoid double-charging when generation and cache write races occur.

End-to-end tests validate scenarios: cache hit same-tenant same-route, cache hit same-tenant different-route (lower tier), cache hit cross-tenant shared cache entry, and concurrent generate+write+rehydrate races. Test asserts both token counts and monetary debits match expected policy.
Observability: trace events emitted on cache write and cache hit with provenance id; Console shows per-hit provenance in the request trace and cost breakdown reflecting normalization decision.

Migration/backfill plan documented: insufficient-provenance entries are marked and either backfilled with best-effort provenance or invalidated to force re-generation within a coordinated rollout window.
tasks: Design schema change: add cache_provenance metadata fields to KV cache entries (generator_model, generator_snapshot, gen_input_tokens, gen_output_tokens, gen_request_id, gen_cost_estimate, tenant_owner)
Add config flag to billing service: cache_cost_normalization_policy (options: original, serving_route, max, deny_cross_tenant)
Runtime: attach provenance to cache writes atomically with ledger write to prevent orphaned entries
Runtime: on cache hit, consult provenance and normalization policy to compute final debit and emit trace
Implement shared-cache tenancy rules: default to deny_cross_tenant or require explicit allowlist; implement per-org opt-in
Backfill: scan cache index for entries missing provenance, mark as 'revalidate-on-hit' and schedule re-generation or eviction
Add unit + integration tests covering token counts, money debits, and race conditions
Add monitoring dashboards: cache-hit-billing-delta, cross-tenant-cache-serves, provenance-missing-rate
Documentation: update billing docs and Console trace UI to show cache provenance and final charged model
Rollout: staged deploy behind feature flag with Canary on internal orgs and synthetic traffic
notes:
Implementation detail proposals: We should prefer storing token-level counts in the cache provenance instead of only byte-length heuristics so the billing calculator can use exact token costs. For shared caches, avoid assigning original tenant as the charged owner; instead either force re-gen or charge the serving tenant using 'max' policy to avoid underbilling. The ledger must record provenance_id as part of the debit record and the cache write must carry a write-intent header (generation_request_id) so we can detect concurrent overlapping writes and ensure only one generation is billed.

Potential risk: Storing extra provenance increases cache entry size; consider compressing the metadata and splitting out a small provenance index table keyed by provenance_id if size becomes problematic. Also ensure KMS/PII review if provenance contains any tenant-identifying metadata.

Open questions:
- Default normalization policy: should it be 'max' to be revenue-safe or 'original' to be customer-friendly?
- For entries produced before rollout (no provenance), should we default to conservative billing (treat as high-cost) or evict?
- How to gracefully handle multi-tenant shared caches in CDNs?
test_plan: Unit tests for billing calculator with provenance payloads
Integration test: simulate generation (write with provenance) followed by cache hit under different serving_route_costs and assert charged_amount matches policy
Race test: concurrent generate+write vs read during heavy load to assert single-billing and ledger anchoring
Backfill test: run backfill job on test cluster and ensure marked entries behave as expected on hit
